meta.title: True Frame — Game-heavy content expansion topic proposals

topics.proposedCardTitleTR: Korsanlar Cumhuriyeti: Nassau (1706–1718)
topics.proposedCardTitleEN: The Republic of Pirates: Nassau (1706–1718)
topics.realWorldAngle: The short-lived pirate haven at Nassau in the Bahamas during the Golden Age of Piracy, its loose self-governance, and how British naval power and pardons dismantled it.
topics.whyItFitsTrueFrame: Black Flag romanticizes a pirate brotherhood; the real frame is a fragile maritime order shaped by trade routes, empire, and labor escaping merchant/navy discipline.
possibleReliableSources: Britannica: Golden Age of Piracy / Edward Teach
Colin Woodard, The Republic of Pirates (academic press)
National Maritime Museum (Royal Museums Greenwich): piracy
topics.duplicateRisk: low — no existing pirate/Black Flag card (existing korsanlar theme is minimal).
topics.notes: Anchor topic for an entire missing franchise (Black Flag).

topics.proposedCardTitleTR: Korsanlık mı, Devlet Hizmeti mi? Privateer Sistemi
topics.proposedCardTitleEN: Privateering vs Piracy: Letters of Marque
topics.realWorldAngle: How states legalized sea raiding via letters of marque, blurring the line between piracy and naval auxiliary in imperial wars.
topics.whyItFitsTrueFrame: The game treats pirates as outlaws; in reality many were state-sanctioned privateers, showing how legality of violence followed political convenience.

topics.proposedCardTitleTR: Karasakal Efsanesi: Edward Thatch'in Gerçeği
topics.proposedCardTitleEN: The Blackbeard Image vs Edward Thatch
topics.realWorldAngle: The deliberate self-branding of Blackbeard (smoking fuses, terror theater) and how reputation was a weapon, versus the thin documentary record of the man.
topics.whyItFitsTrueFrame: A perfect media-vs-reality case: the in-game legend mirrors how Thatch himself manufactured an image that later media amplified.
possibleReliableSources: North Carolina Office of State Archaeology: Queen Anne's Revenge project
topics.notes: Ties image-making to archaeology (QAR shipwreck).

topics.proposedCardTitleTR: Haudenosaunee Konfederasyonu ve Devrim Diplomasisi
topics.proposedCardTitleEN: The Haudenosaunee Confederacy and Revolution-era Diplomacy
topics.realWorldAngle: The Six Nations (Iroquois) Confederacy, its governance, and the impossible diplomatic position of Indigenous nations during the American Revolution.
topics.whyItFitsTrueFrame: Connor's story personalizes a vast political tragedy; the frame is Indigenous sovereignty, alliance, and displacement behind the patriotic war narrative.
possibleReliableSources: Smithsonian National Museum of the American Indian
Library of Congress: American Revolution and Native nations
topics.duplicateRisk: low — no AC III / American Revolution card exists.
topics.notes: Strong, underrepresented region/perspective.

topics.proposedCardTitleTR: Boston Katliamı ve Revere'in Gravürü
topics.proposedCardTitleEN: The Boston Massacre and Revere's Engraving
topics.realWorldAngle: How the 1770 incident became revolutionary propaganda through Paul Revere's misleading engraving, and the trial that followed (John Adams defending the soldiers).
topics.whyItFitsTrueFrame: Direct media-vs-reality: an early example of image manipulation shaping public memory of an event.
possibleReliableSources: Library of Congress: Boston Massacre engraving

topics.proposedCardTitleTR: Yasuke: Nobunaga'nın Hizmetindeki Afrikalı
topics.proposedCardTitleEN: Yasuke: The African Retainer of Oda Nobunaga
topics.realWorldAngle: The documented African man who served Oda Nobunaga in the 1580s, what the limited primary sources actually say, and how myth has inflated the record.
topics.whyItFitsTrueFrame: High-profile, contested topic; the frame separates thin but real documentation from modern dramatization and online mythmaking.
possibleReliableSources: Thomas Lockley & Geoffrey Girard, African Samurai (use cautiously)
Academic Japanese-history journals on Jesuit-era records (Luís Fróis letters)
topics.duplicateRisk: low — feudal Japan exists via Ghost/Shogun but no Yasuke/Shadows card.
topics.notes: Sensitive/contested; emphasize source limits, avoid overclaiming.

topics.proposedCardTitleTR: Tanegashima: Japonya'ya Ateşli Silahın Gelişi
topics.proposedCardTitleEN: Tanegashima: Firearms Arrive in Japan
topics.realWorldAngle: The 1543 Portuguese introduction of matchlock guns, rapid domestic mass-production, and how firearms reshaped Sengoku warfare (e.g., Nagashino).
topics.whyItFitsTrueFrame: Counters the katana-centric samurai image with the decisive role of guns and logistics in unification-era battles.
possibleReliableSources: Metropolitan Museum of Art: Japanese arms and armor
Noel Perrin, Giving Up the Gun (academic discussion)

topics.proposedCardTitleTR: Oda Nobunaga ve Japonya'nın Birleşmesi
topics.proposedCardTitleEN: Oda Nobunaga and the Unification of Japan
topics.realWorldAngle: Nobunaga's military-administrative innovations, treatment of Buddhist power centers, and the messy reality behind the 'ruthless visionary' image.
topics.whyItFitsTrueFrame: The frame is institutional change (markets, castles, religion-state conflict), not just a warlord biography.

topics.proposedCardTitleTR: Samarra ve Gulam Askerler: Halifeliğin Krizi
topics.proposedCardTitleEN: Samarra and the Ghilman: The Abbasid Crisis
topics.realWorldAngle: The 'Anarchy at Samarra' (861–870), the rise of Turkic slave-soldiers (ghilman) as kingmakers, and the fragility of caliphal authority behind Baghdad's golden-age image.
topics.whyItFitsTrueFrame: Mirage centers Baghdad's splendor; the frame is the military-political instability that undercut it, distinct from the existing House of Wisdom cards.
possibleReliableSources: Hugh Kennedy, The Court of the Caliphs (academic)
topics.duplicateRisk: low — distinct from existing ac-mirage-baghdad / house-wisdom-baghdad.
topics.notes: Deliberately avoids the already-covered House of Wisdom / Round City angles.

topics.proposedCardTitleTR: Kuşatma Altında Sivil Hayat: Saraybosna (1992–1996)
topics.proposedCardTitleEN: Civilian Survival Under Siege: Sarajevo (1992–1996)
topics.realWorldAngle: The longest siege of a capital in modern warfare, daily civilian survival (water, fuel, sniper alley), and the explicit inspiration for the game.
topics.whyItFitsTrueFrame: The game's core (ordinary people, not soldiers) maps directly onto documented siege memory and humanitarian records.
possibleReliableSources: ICTY (UN) case records on the Siege of Sarajevo
Galerija 11/07/95 and Historical Museum of BiH
topics.duplicateRisk: low — no civilian-siege/This War of Mine card exists.
topics.notes: Anchor for the missing 'civilian war experience' direction.

topics.proposedCardTitleTR: Hayatta Kalma Ahlakı: Yağma, Paylaşım ve İnsani Hukuk
topics.proposedCardTitleEN: The Ethics of Survival: Scavenging and Humanitarian Law
topics.realWorldAngle: Real dilemmas of civilians in besieged cities and how international humanitarian law (Geneva Conventions) frames protection of non-combatants.
topics.whyItFitsTrueFrame: The game's moral choices connect to a real legal/ethical system rather than abstract 'hard choices'.

topics.proposedCardTitleTR: Sınır Bürokrasisi ve Belge Rejimleri
topics.proposedCardTitleEN: Border Bureaucracy and Document Regimes
topics.realWorldAngle: The 20th-century rise of passports, visas, and checkpoint bureaucracy (esp. Cold War Eastern Bloc) as instruments of state control.
topics.whyItFitsTrueFrame: The fictional Arstotzka stands in for real document regimes; the frame is how paperwork became power.
possibleReliableSources: John Torpey, The Invention of the Passport (Cambridge UP)
League of Nations / interwar passport conference records

topics.proposedCardTitleTR: Gözetim Devleti ve Muhbir Ağları
topics.proposedCardTitleEN: The Surveillance State and Informant Networks
topics.realWorldAngle: How authoritarian states (e.g., the Stasi in the GDR) built mass informant systems, and the bureaucratic banality of repression.
topics.whyItFitsTrueFrame: The game's pressure to comply mirrors documented surveillance regimes; the frame is institutionalized informing.

topics.proposedCardTitleTR: Yazsız Yıl: Tambora ve İklim Felaketi (1816)
topics.proposedCardTitleEN: The Year Without a Summer: Tambora (1816)
topics.realWorldAngle: The 1815 Tambora eruption causing the 1816 global cold/famine, crop failures, migration, and social crisis.
topics.whyItFitsTrueFrame: Frostpunk's frozen-world premise has a real analogue; the frame is how sudden climate shock breaks food and governance systems.
topics.notes: Use 'Çevre' as a new theme (not yet in vocabulary).

topics.proposedCardTitleTR: Olağanüstü Hâl Yönetimi ve Şirket Kasabaları
topics.proposedCardTitleEN: Emergency Governance and Company Towns
topics.realWorldAngle: Historical company towns and crisis governance (rationing, martial order, paternalistic control) during industrial emergencies.
topics.whyItFitsTrueFrame: The game's law-book choices echo real trade-offs between survival, order, and rights in company-run settlements.
possibleReliableSources: Library of Congress: company towns (e.g., Pullman)
National Park Service: Pullman National Monument

topics.proposedCardTitleTR: Psikoz Temsili: Oyun, Tıp ve Damga
topics.proposedCardTitleEN: Representing Psychosis: Game, Medicine, and Stigma
topics.realWorldAngle: The game's collaboration with neuroscientists and people with lived experience to depict psychosis, versus historical stigmatization of mental illness.
topics.whyItFitsTrueFrame: A rare game built on explicit scientific consultation; the frame is psychiatry, lived experience, and the history of 'madness' as moral failing.
possibleReliableSources: Paul Fletcher (University of Cambridge) public talks
topics.notes: Developer collaboration is itself a documented, citable fact.

topics.proposedCardTitleTR: Pikt ve Norse Dünyası: Orkney'de Kültürlerin Kesişimi
topics.proposedCardTitleEN: Picts and Norse: Cultural Collision in Orkney
topics.realWorldAngle: The real Pictish/Norse contact zone in northern Britain and Orkney, and how Norse myth (Hel, the dead) framed worldview.
topics.whyItFitsTrueFrame: The game blends myth and illness; the frame distinguishes archaeological Pict/Norse reality from mythic narrative.
possibleReliableSources: Historic Environment Scotland: Orkney / Pictish sites
topics.duplicateRisk: low — existing viking cards are England/settlement focused.

topics.proposedCardTitleTR: Alman Köylü Savaşı (1525) ve Sınıf Öfkesi
topics.proposedCardTitleEN: The German Peasants' War (1525) and Class Anger
topics.realWorldAngle: The largest popular uprising in Europe before the French Revolution, its religious-economic grievances, and brutal suppression.
topics.whyItFitsTrueFrame: Pentiment's village tensions sit atop a real revolt; the frame is rural class conflict entangled with the Reformation.
topics.duplicateRisk: low — distinct from existing Pentiment printing-press cards.

topics.proposedCardTitleTR: Reform, Endüljans ve Dini Otoritenin Sarsılması
topics.proposedCardTitleEN: Reformation, Indulgences, and Shaken Authority
topics.realWorldAngle: How indulgence sales, print, and Luther's challenge fractured religious authority in the early 16th century.
topics.whyItFitsTrueFrame: Connects the game's manuscript/print theme to the institutional crisis of the Church.
topics.duplicateRisk: medium — pentiment-printing-press touches print culture; keep angle on Church authority/indulgences.

topics.proposedCardTitleTR: Hanedan Evlilikleri: Siyaset Yatak Odasında
topics.proposedCardTitleEN: Dynastic Marriage: Politics in the Bedchamber
topics.realWorldAngle: How medieval/early-modern dynasties used marriage, inheritance law, and legitimacy to build and lose realms (e.g., Habsburg marriage strategy).
topics.whyItFitsTrueFrame: CK3 gamifies succession; the frame is real dynastic statecraft where families were instruments of geopolitics.
possibleReliableSources: Britannica: House of Habsburg / dynastic union
topics.notes: Anchor for the missing Paradox grand-strategy direction.

topics.proposedCardTitleTR: Merkantilizm ve Erken Sömürgecilik
topics.proposedCardTitleEN: Mercantilism and Early Colonialism
topics.realWorldAngle: Early-modern trade nodes, chartered companies, and mercantilist policy that the game abstracts as 'trade power'.
topics.whyItFitsTrueFrame: EU4's map-painting hides real systems of extraction, monopoly, and state-backed commerce.
possibleReliableSources: The National Archives (UK): East India Company
topics.notes: Pairs well with the Obra Dinn / East India Company topic.

topics.proposedCardTitleTR: Sanayileşme, Emek ve Sınıfın Doğuşu
topics.proposedCardTitleEN: Industrialization, Labor, and the Birth of Class
topics.realWorldAngle: 19th-century factory labor, urbanization, child labor, and the emergence of organized labor movements that Victoria 3 models as 'pops' and interest groups.
topics.whyItFitsTrueFrame: The game's economic abstractions rest on real labor history and reform struggles.

topics.proposedCardTitleTR: Topyekûn Savaş Ekonomisi ve Seferberlik
topics.proposedCardTitleEN: Total War Economy and Mobilization
topics.realWorldAngle: How WWII states converted civilian economies to war production (rationing, women in factories, lend-lease) behind the game's 'military factories' abstraction.
topics.whyItFitsTrueFrame: HOI4 reduces war to production sliders; the frame is the social transformation of total mobilization.

topics.proposedCardTitleTR: Sığınağa! Soğuk Savaş Sivil Savunması
topics.proposedCardTitleEN: Duck and Cover: Cold War Civil Defense
topics.realWorldAngle: 1950s–60s US/USSR civil defense (fallout shelters, 'duck and cover' films, CONELRAD) and how it managed public fear of nuclear war.
topics.whyItFitsTrueFrame: Fallout's vault premise satirizes a real culture; the frame is documented civil-defense policy and propaganda.
possibleReliableSources: US National Archives: civil defense films (Duck and Cover)
topics.duplicateRisk: low — existing cold-war cards are proxy-wars/fear-system; this is civil-defense specific.
topics.notes: Anchor for the Fallout franchise.

topics.proposedCardTitleTR: Atom Çağı İyimserliği: 1950'ler Retrofütürizmi
topics.proposedCardTitleEN: Atomic Optimism: 1950s Retrofuturism
topics.realWorldAngle: Postwar atomic optimism (atomic kitchens, 'Atoms for Peace', nuclear-powered everything) versus the risks it downplayed.
topics.whyItFitsTrueFrame: Fallout's aesthetic is a direct satire of a real cultural moment; the frame is the gap between atomic hype and reality.
possibleReliableSources: Smithsonian / National Museum of American History

topics.proposedCardTitleTR: Vault Deneyleri ve İnsan Üzerinde Araştırma Etiği
topics.proposedCardTitleEN: Vault Experiments and Research Ethics
topics.realWorldAngle: Real unethical human experiments (Tuskegee, Cold War radiation studies) and the rise of informed-consent ethics (Nuremberg Code, Belmont Report).
topics.whyItFitsTrueFrame: The vaults' secret experiments parody documented abuses; the frame is the history of research ethics.
possibleReliableSources: US Dept. of Energy: ACHRE (radiation experiments report)
topics.notes: Sensitive; handle factually.

topics.proposedCardTitleTR: Gözetim Kapitalizmi: Veri Yeni Petrol mü?
topics.proposedCardTitleEN: Surveillance Capitalism: Is Data the New Oil?
topics.realWorldAngle: The real economics of data extraction, behavioral targeting, and the concept of surveillance capitalism behind Night City's corporate dystopia.
topics.whyItFitsTrueFrame: 2077 is fiction, but its corporate-data world maps to documented business models and privacy debates.
possibleReliableSources: EU GDPR official texts / European Data Protection Board
topics.notes: Anchor for a near-future tech-politics direction.

topics.proposedCardTitleTR: Şirket Egemenliği: Devlet Gibi Davranan Şirketler
topics.proposedCardTitleEN: Corporate Sovereignty: When Companies Act Like States
topics.realWorldAngle: Historical precedents for corporations exercising state-like power (East India Company, company towns, modern corporate enclaves).
topics.whyItFitsTrueFrame: Night City's megacorps echo real cases where firms held quasi-sovereign authority.
possibleReliableSources: The National Archives (UK): East India Company

topics.proposedCardTitleTR: Lojistik Medeniyeti Kurar: Yollar, Posta ve Taşıyıcılar
topics.proposedCardTitleEN: Logistics Builds Civilization: Roads, Mail, and Porters
topics.realWorldAngle: How postal systems, road networks, and porterage (e.g., Inca chasqui runners, early postal relays) literally held states together.
topics.whyItFitsTrueFrame: The game makes delivery heroic; the frame is the real, under-celebrated history of infrastructure and logistics as state power.
topics.notes: Pairs with existing 'messengers' history without duplicating a specific war card.

topics.proposedCardTitleTR: Karşılıklı Yok Oluş: Nükleer Caydırıcılık Mantığı
topics.proposedCardTitleEN: Mutual Assured Destruction: The Logic of Deterrence
topics.realWorldAngle: Cold War deterrence theory (MAD), the arms race, and near-miss incidents (e.g., 1983 Petrov / Able Archer) behind Metal Gear's anti-nuke themes.
topics.whyItFitsTrueFrame: MGS is explicitly about nukes; the frame is the real strategic doctrine and the human fragility of the system.
topics.duplicateRisk: low — distinct from Oppenheimer/Manhattan cards (doctrine, not the bomb's creation).
topics.notes: Anchor for the MGS franchise (currently only a combo card).

topics.proposedCardTitleTR: Özel Askeri Şirketler: Savaşın Taşeronlaşması
topics.proposedCardTitleEN: Private Military Companies: Outsourcing War
topics.realWorldAngle: The modern rise of PMCs and the long history of mercenaries (condottieri, Hessians), and the accountability gaps they create.
topics.whyItFitsTrueFrame: MGS's 'soldiers without borders' reflects a real, growing privatization of force.
possibleReliableSources: ICRC: private military and security companies (Montreux Document)
Geneva Centre for Security Sector Governance (DCAF)

topics.proposedCardTitleTR: Ahlaki Yara: Savaş Travması ve Kahraman Anlatısının Eleştirisi
topics.proposedCardTitleEN: Moral Injury: War Trauma and the Critique of Heroic Shooters
topics.realWorldAngle: The clinical concepts of PTSD and 'moral injury', and the laws/ethics around weapons like white phosphorus.
topics.whyItFitsTrueFrame: The game critiques the shooter genre; the frame is real military psychology and the law of armed conflict.
possibleReliableSources: US Dept. of Veterans Affairs: PTSD / moral injury
topics.notes: Spoiler major because the game's twist is the point; frame around real concepts, not plot.

topics.proposedCardTitleTR: Dubai'yi Kim İnşa Etti? Göçmen İşçiler ve Kentin Yükselişi
topics.proposedCardTitleEN: Who Built Dubai? Migrant Labor and the Vertical City
topics.realWorldAngle: Dubai's rapid construction boom, migrant labor conditions (kafala system debates), and the engineering of a desert megacity.
topics.whyItFitsTrueFrame: The game's buried Dubai is a backdrop; the frame is the real labor and infrastructure story behind such cities.
possibleReliableSources: ILO: labour migration in the Gulf
Human Rights Watch / Amnesty International reports (NGO)
topics.notes: Use NGO sources carefully and attribute clearly.

topics.proposedCardTitleTR: Arkeoloji mi, Yağma mı? Müzeler ve Eserlerin İadesi
topics.proposedCardTitleEN: Archaeology vs Looting: Museums and Repatriation
topics.realWorldAngle: The difference between scientific archaeology and looting, the antiquities trade, and modern repatriation debates (e.g., Parthenon Marbles, Benin Bronzes).
topics.whyItFitsTrueFrame: Lara Croft embodies the 'adventurer grabs treasure' myth; the frame is real archaeological ethics and colonial collecting.
topics.duplicateRisk: low — existing Alexandria-library archaeology angle is event-specific, not the ethics of looting.
topics.notes: Anchor for Tomb Raider/Uncharted adventure-archaeology critique.

topics.proposedCardTitleTR: Maceracı Miti: Lost City Hikâyeleri ve Sömürgeci Bakış
topics.proposedCardTitleEN: The Adventurer Myth: 'Lost Cities' and the Colonial Gaze
topics.realWorldAngle: How 'lost city' legends (El Dorado, Z) emerged from colonial-era exploration, and what real expeditions and modern remote-sensing find instead.
topics.whyItFitsTrueFrame: Nathan Drake is the pulp-explorer fantasy; the frame is the history of exploration narratives and their distortions.

topics.proposedCardTitleTR: Kara Ölüm (1347–1351): Neden ve Sonuçlar
topics.proposedCardTitleEN: The Black Death (1347–1351): Causes and Consequences
topics.realWorldAngle: The mid-14th-century plague pandemic, Yersinia pestis, mortality scale, and its social/economic aftershocks (labor, wages, religion).
topics.whyItFitsTrueFrame: The game's plague-and-rats horror sits on real pandemic history, distinct from the 1665 Great Plague card already in the app.
possibleReliableSources: Ole J. Benedictow, The Black Death (academic)
topics.duplicateRisk: medium — existing london-fire-plague is 1665; clearly date/scope this as 1347 pandemic.
topics.notes: Anchor for A Plague Tale.

topics.proposedCardTitleTR: Fareler mi Suçlu? Veba Bulaşma Tartışması
topics.proposedCardTitleEN: Are Rats to Blame? The Plague Transmission Debate
topics.realWorldAngle: The classic rat-flea transmission model versus newer research on human ectoparasites and pneumonic spread.
topics.whyItFitsTrueFrame: The game makes rats the literal threat; the frame is a live scientific debate about how plague actually spread.
topics.notes: Great 'misconception' card.

topics.proposedCardTitleTR: Yasak Bölge: Çernobil Tahliyesi ve Pripyat'ın Boşalması
topics.proposedCardTitleEN: The Exclusion Zone: Chernobyl Evacuation and Empty Pripyat
topics.realWorldAngle: The 1986 evacuation, the creation and management of the Chernobyl Exclusion Zone, abandoned Pripyat, returnees (samosely), and wildlife recovery.
topics.whyItFitsTrueFrame: The game's Zone is fictionalized; the frame is the real, ongoing geography and human story of the exclusion zone, distinct from the disaster's cause.
topics.duplicateRisk: medium — existing chernobyl-disaster/chernobyl-secrecy are about the accident; focus this on the Zone/resettlement.
topics.notes: Clearly differentiate from existing Chernobyl cards.

topics.proposedCardTitleTR: Felaket Turizmi: Çernobil'i Gezmek Etik mi?
topics.proposedCardTitleEN: Dark Tourism: Is Visiting Chernobyl Ethical?
topics.realWorldAngle: The growth of dark/disaster tourism to Chernobyl (amplified by media), and debates about memory, voyeurism, and respect.
topics.whyItFitsTrueFrame: The game helped mythologize the Zone; the frame is how disaster sites become tourist and media products.

topics.proposedCardTitleTR: Çanakkale: Gelibolu Kara Savaşları (1915)
topics.proposedCardTitleEN: Gallipoli: The 1915 Land Campaign
topics.realWorldAngle: The failed Allied Gallipoli campaign, Ottoman defense, ANZAC memory, and the brutal stalemate of the Dardanelles front.
topics.whyItFitsTrueFrame: BF1 showcases lesser-known fronts; Gallipoli is hugely significant in Turkish, ANZAC, and Ottoman history.
topics.duplicateRisk: low — high local (TR) relevance and not yet covered.
topics.notes: Strong resonance for a Turkish-first audience.

topics.proposedCardTitleTR: Arap İsyanı ve Lawrence Efsanesi
topics.proposedCardTitleEN: The Arab Revolt and the Lawrence Myth
topics.realWorldAngle: The WWI Arab Revolt against the Ottomans, T.E. Lawrence's actual vs mythologized role, and the broken promises of the postwar settlement.
topics.whyItFitsTrueFrame: BF1's desert chapter dramatizes Lawrence; the frame separates the man from the legend and the politics of Sykes-Picot.

topics.proposedCardTitleTR: Unutulan Askerler: Sömürge Birlikleri (Tirailleurs)
topics.proposedCardTitleEN: The Forgotten Soldiers: Colonial Troops (Tirailleurs)
topics.realWorldAngle: The role of colonial and African troops in the French and Allied armies, their erasure from postwar memory, and events like Thiaroye.
topics.whyItFitsTrueFrame: BF V's 'untold stories' framing matches a real gap in WWII memory about colonial soldiers.
topics.notes: Pairs thematically with existing Harlem Hellfighters card but distinct war/units.

topics.proposedCardTitleTR: Ağır Su Sabotajı: Norveç ve Nazi Atom Programı
topics.proposedCardTitleEN: The Heavy Water Sabotage: Norway and the Nazi Atomic Program
topics.realWorldAngle: The 1943 Norwegian resistance sabotage of the Vemork heavy-water plant and its role in hampering Nazi nuclear research.
topics.whyItFitsTrueFrame: BF V's Nordlys chapter dramatizes a real, decisive resistance operation.

topics.proposedCardTitleTR: Stalingrad: Şehir Savaşı ve Keskin Nişancı Miti
topics.proposedCardTitleEN: Stalingrad: Urban Warfare and the Sniper Myth
topics.realWorldAngle: The 1942–43 Battle of Stalingrad, the reality of urban attrition, and the propaganda/mythology around snipers like Vasily Zaitsev.
topics.whyItFitsTrueFrame: CoD/Enemy at the Gates popularized the sniper duel; the frame is the documented battle vs propaganda legend.

topics.proposedCardTitleTR: MKUltra: CIA'nın Zihin Kontrolü Programı
topics.proposedCardTitleEN: MKUltra: The CIA's Mind-Control Program
topics.realWorldAngle: The real CIA MKUltra experiments (LSD, coercive interrogation), their exposure (Church Committee), and the ethics fallout.
topics.whyItFitsTrueFrame: Black Ops centers brainwashing; MKUltra is the documented program behind the trope.
possibleReliableSources: US National Archives / Church Committee report

topics.proposedCardTitleTR: Domuzlar Körfezi: Başarısız Bir Gizli Operasyon
topics.proposedCardTitleEN: The Bay of Pigs: An Operation That Failed
topics.realWorldAngle: The 1961 CIA-backed invasion of Cuba, its failure, and its role in escalating the Cold War toward the Missile Crisis.
topics.whyItFitsTrueFrame: Black Ops uses Cuban operations as set-pieces; the frame is the documented covert history.

topics.proposedCardTitleTR: Cu Chi Tünelleri: Yeraltında Vietnam Savaşı
topics.proposedCardTitleEN: The Cu Chi Tunnels: The Vietnam War Underground
topics.realWorldAngle: The vast Viet Cong tunnel networks, asymmetric warfare, and the civilian-military reality of the Vietnam War.
topics.whyItFitsTrueFrame: Vietnam shooters flatten the war into spectacle; the frame is asymmetric tactics and the human cost.
possibleReliableSources: Britannica: Vietnam War / Cu Chi tunnels

topics.proposedCardTitleTR: Savaş Sonrası Amerika: GI Bill, Banliyö ve Refah
topics.proposedCardTitleEN: Postwar America: The GI Bill, Suburbs, and Prosperity
topics.realWorldAngle: The post-WWII US boom: the GI Bill, suburbanization, consumer credit, and the uneven access (redlining) behind the 'American Dream'.
topics.whyItFitsTrueFrame: Mafia II's 1940s-50s setting frames the era as gangster backdrop; the real frame is the social engineering of postwar prosperity.
possibleReliableSources: Library of Congress: redlining / HOLC maps
topics.duplicateRisk: low — existing Mafia cards are Prohibition/immigration/RICO.

topics.proposedCardTitleTR: Kara Yıldız Cinayeti ve Tabloid Basının Doğuşu
topics.proposedCardTitleEN: The Black Dahlia and the Rise of Tabloid Crime
topics.realWorldAngle: The 1947 Elizabeth Short murder, the sensationalist press that fed on it, and how unsolved true crime became mass entertainment.
topics.whyItFitsTrueFrame: L.A. Noire's cases echo real LA crime; the frame is the media ecosystem that turned victims into spectacle.
topics.duplicateRisk: low — distinct from existing policing/postwar-trauma L.A. Noire cards.
topics.notes: Frame around media, not graphic detail.

topics.proposedCardTitleTR: Ahlaki Panik: Medya, Şiddet ve 'Tehlikeli Oyunlar' Korkusu
topics.proposedCardTitleEN: Moral Panic: Media, Violence, and 'Dangerous Games'
topics.realWorldAngle: The history of moral panics (comics, pinball, rock, video games), the sociology of moral panic (Cohen), and what research actually says about media effects.
topics.whyItFitsTrueFrame: GTA is the perennial scapegoat; the frame is a well-studied recurring social phenomenon.
possibleReliableSources: Stanley Cohen, Folk Devils and Moral Panics (academic)
APA statements on media violence research
topics.notes: Self-aware, meta topic that fits True Frame's mission well.

topics.proposedCardTitleTR: Şirket, Gemi, Sigorta: Doğu Hindistan Ticareti ve Lloyd's
topics.proposedCardTitleEN: Company, Ship, Insurance: East India Trade and Lloyd's
topics.realWorldAngle: Early-modern maritime trade companies, the dangers of long voyages, and the birth of marine insurance (Lloyd's of London) to manage catastrophic risk.
topics.whyItFitsTrueFrame: The game is literally an insurance investigation of a lost ship; the frame is the real machinery of maritime trade and risk.
possibleReliableSources: The National Archives (UK): East India Company
topics.notes: Unusually clean media-to-frame mapping (insurance adjuster premise).

topics.proposedCardTitleTR: İran Devrimi (1979): Bir Rejimin Çöküşü
topics.proposedCardTitleEN: The Iranian Revolution (1979): A Regime Falls
topics.realWorldAngle: The 1979 revolution, the fall of the Shah, mass mobilization, and the contested memory of events like Black Friday.
topics.whyItFitsTrueFrame: Built by people who lived/researched it; the game uses real photos/footage as a deliberate documentary frame.
topics.duplicateRisk: low — no modern Iran/1979 card exists.
topics.notes: Underrepresented region; pairs with the Argo film proposal.

topics.proposedCardTitleTR: Teknoloji Ağacı Miti: Tarih Bir Merdiven mi?
topics.proposedCardTitleEN: The Tech Tree Myth: Is History a Ladder?
topics.realWorldAngle: How the 'tech tree' implies inevitable, linear progress, versus contingency, lost technologies, and parallel non-Western innovation.
topics.whyItFitsTrueFrame: A core gameplay abstraction becomes a teachable misconception about how technology actually develops.
possibleReliableSources: Academic STS (e.g., David Edgerton, The Shock of the Old)
topics.duplicateRisk: medium — civ-linear-history & civ-great-leaders exist; keep this strictly on the tech-tree mechanic.
topics.notes: Strong meta-history card; ensure distinct from civ-linear-history.

topics.proposedCardTitleTR: Kuşatma Mühendisliği: Mancınık, Trebüşe ve Surların Sonu
topics.proposedCardTitleEN: Siege Engineering: Trebuchets and the End of Walls
topics.realWorldAngle: The real engineering of medieval siege weapons (torsion vs counterweight), logistics of sieges, and how gunpowder ended high medieval walls.
topics.whyItFitsTrueFrame: AoE abstracts siege units; the frame is the physics, labor, and supply behind besieging a city.
topics.duplicateRisk: medium — total-war-siege-starvation exists; angle on engineering/mechanics, not starvation.

topics.proposedCardTitleTR: Paralı Ordular: Condottieri ve Savaşın Ekonomisi
topics.proposedCardTitleEN: Armies for Hire: Condottieri and the Economy of War
topics.realWorldAngle: Renaissance Italian mercenary captains (condottieri), contracts, and how city-states outsourced war finance and risk.
topics.whyItFitsTrueFrame: Total War lets you buy mercenaries instantly; the frame is the real market and politics of hired armies.
possibleReliableSources: The Metropolitan Museum of Art (Renaissance Italy)

topics.proposedCardTitleTR: Orta Çağ Bohemya'sında Salgın ve Karantina Önlemleri
topics.proposedCardTitleEN: Epidemic and Quarantine in Medieval Bohemia
topics.realWorldAngle: How medieval communities responded to epidemics (isolation, cordon, religious processions, miasma theory) before germ theory.
topics.whyItFitsTrueFrame: KCD's grounded daily life is a natural frame for real medieval public-health practice.
topics.duplicateRisk: medium — many KCD daily-life cards exist; keep tightly scoped to epidemic response.

topics.proposedCardTitleTR: Feodal Orduyu Beslemek: Vasal, Tımar ve Sefer Ekonomisi
topics.proposedCardTitleEN: Feeding a Feudal Army: Vassals, Fiefs, and Campaign Economy
topics.realWorldAngle: How real feudal/early-modern rulers raised, paid, and supplied armies (levies, retinues, the limits of feudal service days).
topics.whyItFitsTrueFrame: Bannerlord models recruitment/economy; the frame is the genuine constraints that shaped medieval campaigns.
topics.duplicateRisk: low — Bannerlord world is fictional but mechanics map to real feudal systems.
topics.notes: Note the fictional Calradia setting; frame on real feudal logistics.

topics.proposedCardTitleTR: 1918 Grip Pandemisi: Londra ve Görünmeyen Düşman
topics.proposedCardTitleEN: The 1918 Influenza Pandemic: London and the Invisible Enemy
topics.realWorldAngle: The 1918–19 influenza pandemic, its staggering toll, wartime censorship of news, and public-health response in cities like London.
topics.whyItFitsTrueFrame: Vampyr is set in flu-stricken 1918 London; the supernatural plot sits on a very real catastrophe.
topics.duplicateRisk: low — distinct era from Black Death / 1665 plague cards.

topics.proposedCardTitleTR: Bir Kasaba Nasıl Doğar? Burgage Parselleri ve Ortak Topraklar
topics.proposedCardTitleEN: How a Town Is Born: Burgage Plots and Common Land
topics.realWorldAngle: Real medieval town formation: burgage plots, market charters, the open-field system, and common land before enclosure.
topics.whyItFitsTrueFrame: Manor Lords is praised for authentic town-building; the frame is the actual property and agricultural systems it models.
topics.duplicateRisk: medium — overlaps KCD daily-life/markets; angle on town/land tenure systems.

topics.proposedCardTitleTR: Şövalyelik Miti: Onurlu Düello mu, Kanlı Pragmatizm mi?
topics.proposedCardTitleEN: The Chivalry Myth: Honorable Duel or Bloody Pragmatism?
topics.realWorldAngle: The gap between the literary ideal of chivalry and the brutal reality of medieval combat, ransom economics, and treatment of non-nobles.
topics.whyItFitsTrueFrame: For Honor pits idealized knights/vikings/samurai; the frame is how 'honor codes' often masked pragmatic, unequal violence.
possibleReliableSources: Academic studies on medieval warfare and ransom
topics.duplicateRisk: medium — samurai-honor cards exist; angle on European chivalry + cross-cultural comparison.

topics.proposedCardTitleTR: Sanayi Şehri: Duman, Gecekondu ve Halk Sağlığı
topics.proposedCardTitleEN: The Industrial City: Smoke, Slums, and Public Health
topics.realWorldAngle: 19th-century industrial urbanization, sanitation crises (cholera, the Great Stink), and the birth of modern public-health infrastructure.
topics.whyItFitsTrueFrame: Anno 1800 gamifies industrial city-building; the frame is the real human and sanitary cost that drove reform.

topics.proposedCardTitleTR: Kale Sadece Savunma Değil: Bir Ekonomik Motor
topics.proposedCardTitleEN: A Castle Is Not Just Defense: It's an Economic Engine
topics.realWorldAngle: Castles as administrative, economic, and symbolic centers (food stores, lordship, justice), not merely military forts.
topics.whyItFitsTrueFrame: Stronghold ties castle to food/economy; the frame is the real multifunction role of castles, complementing the existing AoE2 castle-politics card.
topics.duplicateRisk: medium — aoe2-castles-politics exists; angle on castle-as-economy/admin, not politics.

topics.proposedCardTitleTR: Bletchley Park: Enigma'yı Kırmak ve Turing'in Gerçeği
topics.proposedCardTitleEN: Bletchley Park: Breaking Enigma and the Real Turing
topics.realWorldAngle: The collective codebreaking effort at Bletchley Park (incl. Polish cryptologists and many women), the bombe, and the film's compressions/distortions of Turing's life.
topics.whyItFitsTrueFrame: The film centers a lone genius; the frame is a large, collaborative intelligence operation and the real history of computing and Turing's persecution.

topics.proposedCardTitleTR: Gizli Kahramanlar: NASA, Ayrımcılık ve Hesap Makineleri
topics.proposedCardTitleEN: Hidden Figures: NASA, Segregation, and Human Computers
topics.realWorldAngle: The Black women mathematicians at NACA/NASA (Katherine Johnson et al.), segregation-era labor, and the transition to electronic computing.
topics.whyItFitsTrueFrame: The film dramatizes real people; the frame is the documented history of segregation, labor, and the space race.
possibleReliableSources: Smithsonian National Air and Space Museum

topics.mediaTitle: All Quiet on the Western Front (2022)
topics.gameOrMediaFranchise: All Quiet on the Western Front
topics.proposedCardTitleTR: Batı Cephesinde Yeni Bir Şey Yok: Savaşın Anlamsızlığı
topics.proposedCardTitleEN: All Quiet on the Western Front: The Futility of War
topics.realWorldAngle: The German WWI experience, trench attrition, the armistice's final hours, and the anti-war literary tradition (Remarque).
topics.whyItFitsTrueFrame: Complements existing 1917/Valiant Hearts cards with the German perspective and the politics of the armistice.
possibleReliableSources: Britannica: Erich Maria Remarque / Western Front
topics.duplicateRisk: medium — several WWI cards exist; angle on German side + armistice.

topics.mediaTitle: Master and Commander: The Far Side of the World
topics.proposedCardTitleTR: Yelkenli Çağında Donanma Hayatı: Napolyon Savaşları'nda Royal Navy
topics.proposedCardTitleEN: Naval Life in the Age of Sail: The Napoleonic Royal Navy
topics.realWorldAngle: Daily life, discipline, scurvy/health, and tactics aboard Royal Navy ships during the Napoleonic Wars.
topics.whyItFitsTrueFrame: The film is praised for authenticity; the frame is the real social and medical world of the age of sail.

topics.proposedCardTitleTR: Son Düello: Orta Çağ'da Adalet, Tanıklık ve Kadının Sözü
topics.proposedCardTitleEN: The Last Duel: Medieval Justice and a Woman's Testimony
topics.realWorldAngle: The 1386 judicial duel in France, trial by combat as legal procedure, and the legal status of women's testimony in medieval courts.
topics.whyItFitsTrueFrame: Based on a documented case; the frame is the medieval justice system and gendered law, not just the spectacle.

topics.proposedCardTitleTR: Tetris: Soğuk Savaş, Sovyet Yazılımı ve Telif Savaşı
topics.proposedCardTitleEN: Tetris: Cold War, Soviet Software, and an IP Battle
topics.realWorldAngle: The real story of Tetris's creation in the USSR, state ownership of software, and the tangled international licensing fight.
topics.whyItFitsTrueFrame: A film about a game becomes a frame for Soviet economics, intellectual property, and the late Cold War.

topics.proposedCardTitleTR: Argo: İran Rehine Krizi ve Gerçeğin Dramatizasyonu
topics.proposedCardTitleEN: Argo: The Iran Hostage Crisis and Dramatized Truth
topics.realWorldAngle: The 1979–81 hostage crisis, the 'Canadian Caper' rescue, and the film's well-documented exaggerations (e.g., the airport chase).
topics.whyItFitsTrueFrame: A clear media-vs-reality case where a true event was reshaped for tension; complements the 1979 Revolution game topic.

topics.proposedCardTitleTR: 12 Yıllık Esaret: Kölelik, Tanıklık ve İlga Mücadelesi
topics.proposedCardTitleEN: 12 Years a Slave: Slavery, Testimony, and Abolition
topics.realWorldAngle: Solomon Northup's real 1853 memoir, the slave system of the antebellum US South, and the abolition movement.
topics.whyItFitsTrueFrame: Based on a primary-source memoir; the frame is the documented institution of slavery and the value of firsthand testimony.
possibleReliableSources: Smithsonian National Museum of African American History and Culture
topics.notes: Add 'Kölelik' as a theme (slavery exists thematically via tf26 but not named).

topics.proposedCardTitleTR: Ruanda Soykırımı: Hafıza, Medya ve Uluslararası Sessizlik
topics.proposedCardTitleEN: The Rwandan Genocide: Memory, Media, and International Silence
topics.realWorldAngle: The 1994 genocide, the role of radio propaganda (RTLM), international inaction, and contested aspects of the film's narrative.
topics.whyItFitsTrueFrame: The film personalizes a vast atrocity; the frame is documented genocide history, propaganda, and memory politics.
possibleReliableSources: UN / ICTR (International Criminal Tribunal for Rwanda)
topics.notes: Sensitive; rely on tribunal and memorial sources.

topics.proposedCardTitleTR: Çöküş: Berlin'in Düşüşü ve Nazi Rejiminin Son Günleri
topics.proposedCardTitleEN: Downfall: The Fall of Berlin and the Regime's Last Days
topics.realWorldAngle: The 1945 Battle of Berlin, the Führerbunker, and debates about depicting Hitler's humanity without enabling sympathy.
topics.whyItFitsTrueFrame: Based on eyewitness accounts; the frame is the documented end of the Reich and the ethics of representation.

topics.proposedCardTitleTR: Apollo 13: Başarılı Bir Başarısızlık ve Mühendislik Krizi
topics.proposedCardTitleEN: Apollo 13: A Successful Failure and Engineering Under Pressure
topics.realWorldAngle: The 1970 in-flight explosion, the improvised CO2 scrubber fix, and the systems-engineering culture that saved the crew.
topics.whyItFitsTrueFrame: Largely faithful film; the frame is real crisis engineering and NASA process, complementing existing space cards.
possibleReliableSources: Smithsonian National Air and Space Museum
topics.duplicateRisk: medium — space cards exist (Apollo 11); scope to Apollo 13 crisis engineering.

topics.proposedCardTitleTR: Casus Takası: U-2 Olayı ve Soğuk Savaş Diplomasisi
topics.proposedCardTitleEN: The Spy Swap: The U-2 Incident and Cold War Diplomacy
topics.realWorldAngle: The 1960 U-2 shootdown, the Powers/Abel prisoner exchange, and back-channel Cold War diplomacy.
topics.whyItFitsTrueFrame: Based on real events; the frame is documented espionage and the legal-diplomatic machinery of the Cold War.
possibleReliableSources: CIA FOIA reading room: U-2 program

topics.proposedCardTitleTR: Savaştan Dönenler: WWI Sonrası Birmingham ve Sanayi Çeteleri
topics.proposedCardTitleEN: Coming Home from War: Post-WWI Birmingham and Industrial Gangs
topics.realWorldAngle: Post-WWI veteran trauma and unemployment, the real (earlier) Peaky Blinders street gangs, and industrial Birmingham's class world.
topics.whyItFitsTrueFrame: The show stylizes a real city and era; the frame is veteran reintegration, labor unrest, and street-gang history.

topics.proposedCardTitleTR: Kokain Ticareti ve Uyuşturucu Savaşı: Escobar Efsanesinin Ötesi
topics.proposedCardTitleEN: The Cocaine Trade and the Drug War: Beyond the Escobar Legend
topics.realWorldAngle: The political economy of the cocaine trade, the US-led 'War on Drugs', and the contested memory of Pablo Escobar in Colombia.
topics.whyItFitsTrueFrame: Narcos blends fact and dramatization; the frame is the documented economics and politics of the drug war.
possibleReliableSources: Britannica: Pablo Escobar / War on Drugs

topics.proposedCardTitleTR: Derin Casuslar: Soğuk Savaş'ta KGB 'İllegalleri'
topics.proposedCardTitleEN: Deep-Cover Spies: KGB 'Illegals' in the Cold War
topics.realWorldAngle: The real KGB 'illegals' program (deep-cover agents), exposed networks (e.g., the 2010 Illegals Program), and counterintelligence.
topics.whyItFitsTrueFrame: The show fictionalizes a documented espionage method; the frame is the reality of deep-cover intelligence.
possibleReliableSources: US FBI history / DOJ (2010 Illegals case)

topics.proposedCardTitleTR: Patronaj ve Politika: Geç Roma Cumhuriyeti'nin Çöküşü
topics.proposedCardTitleEN: Patronage and Politics: The Fall of the Late Roman Republic
topics.realWorldAngle: The patron-client system, populares vs optimates, and how the Republic's institutions failed into civil war and one-man rule.
topics.whyItFitsTrueFrame: Rome dramatizes elite intrigue; the frame is the real institutional collapse, distinct from the existing Colosseum/empire-decline cards.
topics.duplicateRisk: medium — Roman cards exist; scope to Republic's political institutions/patronage.

topics.proposedCardTitleTR: Kubilay Han'ın Sarayı: Yuan Yönetimi ve İpek Yolu Diplomasisi
topics.proposedCardTitleEN: Kublai Khan's Court: Yuan Administration and Silk Road Diplomacy
topics.realWorldAngle: The Yuan dynasty's governance of China, the reliability debate around Marco Polo's account, and Silk Road exchange.
topics.whyItFitsTrueFrame: The show uses a contested travelogue; the frame is Mongol-Yuan administration and the historiography of Polo's text.
possibleReliableSources: Britannica: Kublai Khan / Yuan dynasty / Marco Polo
topics.duplicateRisk: medium — Silk Road & Mongol cards exist; scope to Yuan court + Polo source-reliability.

topics.proposedCardTitleTR: 1066: Stamford Köprüsü ve Viking Çağı'nın Sonu
topics.proposedCardTitleEN: 1066: Stamford Bridge and the End of the Viking Age
topics.realWorldAngle: The 1066 Norwegian invasion under Harald Hardrada, the Battle of Stamford Bridge, and how it set up Hastings weeks later.
topics.whyItFitsTrueFrame: The show dramatizes the late Viking Age; the frame is the pivotal 1066 campaigns, distinct from existing settlement/raid cards.
possibleReliableSources: Britannica: Battle of Stamford Bridge / Harald III
topics.duplicateRisk: low — distinct event from existing viking cards.

topics.proposedCardTitleTR: Atlantik Savaşı: U-Bot Hayatı ve Konvoy Mücadelesi
topics.proposedCardTitleEN: The Battle of the Atlantic: U-Boat Life and the Convoy War
topics.realWorldAngle: The WWII Battle of the Atlantic, brutal U-boat service conditions, convoy/ASDIC tactics, and codebreaking's role.
topics.whyItFitsTrueFrame: Das Boot is famed for realism; the frame is the decisive, attritional naval campaign and its technology.

topics.proposedCardTitleTR: Savaş Afişleri: Devletler Kamuoyunu Nasıl Şekillendirdi?
topics.proposedCardTitleEN: War Posters: How States Shaped Public Opinion
topics.realWorldAngle: The visual language of WWI/WWII propaganda posters (recruitment, rationing, enemy imagery) and how mass persuasion was engineered.
topics.whyItFitsTrueFrame: A general card on the documented craft of state propaganda imagery, useful across many war-themed media.
possibleReliableSources: US Library of Congress / National Archives poster archives
topics.duplicateRisk: low — propaganda is a theme but no dedicated posters card.

topics.proposedCardTitleTR: Rum Ateşi: Bizans'ın Gizli Silahı ve Kayıp Teknoloji
topics.proposedCardTitleEN: Greek Fire: Byzantium's Secret Weapon and a Lost Technology
topics.realWorldAngle: The incendiary weapon 'Greek fire', the state secrecy that protected its formula, and why the recipe was ultimately lost.
topics.whyItFitsTrueFrame: A general card on technology, secrecy, and how knowledge can disappear — counters the 'tech only advances' assumption.
topics.notes: Pairs conceptually with the Civilization tech-tree card.

topics.proposedCardTitleTR: Haritalar Yalan Söyler mi? Kartografya ve İktidar
topics.proposedCardTitleEN: Do Maps Lie? Cartography and Power
topics.realWorldAngle: How map projections, borders, and naming encode political choices (Mercator distortions, propaganda maps, contested borders).
topics.whyItFitsTrueFrame: A general card decoding the maps players/viewers take for granted in strategy games and media.
possibleReliableSources: Library of Congress: Geography & Map Division
topics.notes: Add 'Coğrafya' as a new theme.

topics.proposedCardTitleTR: Saat Kaç? Demiryolları ve Standart Zamanın İcadı
topics.proposedCardTitleEN: What Time Is It? Railways and the Invention of Standard Time
topics.realWorldAngle: How railways forced the standardization of local time into time zones (railway time, 1884 Prime Meridian conference).
topics.whyItFitsTrueFrame: A general card showing how a now-invisible system (clock time) was a 19th-century technological-political construction.
possibleReliableSources: Britannica: standard time / International Meridian Conference
